summary:
Still Out There -
The machines we sent to other worlds, and never brought home.

This project was developed as a story, starting from earth in 1967 all the way to 2020, each and every hardware designed by NASA has been put and adjusted in a timeline so kids and adults could learn what each of them did like the Apollo 11 launch pad gimmick, or how Pheonix found ice for the first time in mars.
details:
Still Out There

Still Out There is a 3D Interactive Story-Telling Website about the machines NASA sent out to other planets and never brought back home. Our project goes around every one starting from the oldest in 1967, all the way to the newest hardware being sent out in 2020. The benefits gained from this are crucial, both Kids & Adults could learn alot of new information using our website, whether it is finding out the reason behind Apollo 11, Kepler Telscope, or the Lunar Roving Vehicles function. Our project "Still Out There" provides and talks about all of these inventions, how great they were, their functions, their purpouse, and how they managed to pull each one off, in a way thats engaging and attractive to all ages. This could steer alot of attention to kids specifically and engage them in Astronomy / Physics which in the future will result to a new generation of intelligence. All beginning from this very timeline. Our goal is to impact the future generations interest, by presenting them the "retired" missions of NASA. We used a dopamine intuitive 'One continuous flight through time and space where each machine speaks for itself' to catch the readers attention. Each 3D model of the hardware (except for 5 models which were portrayed using code) is provided by NASA's resources itself where we used those to show the world how interesting and unique each machinery has for itself. On the technical side we used three.js (including its post-processing examples used for motion blur), React, React Three Fiber, drei, troika-three-text (3D text, via drei), Lenis, Vite, Tailwind CSS (licensed by MIT), GSAP + ScrollTrigger (GSAP standard licence (free, including commercial use)), Draco decoder (from three.js, in public/draco/) (Apache 2.0), Space Grotesk, Space Mono (via Fontsource, self-hosted) (SIL Open Font License 1.1).
